correctness.rationale: PASS: Polarization reduces the norm identity to 16 exact complex bidegree moments sum w z^j zbar^k=j!delta_jk for 0<=j,k<=3. At N<=5, a nonzero real quadratic Q vanishes on all nodes. Integrating Q,Qz,Q zbar and Q(|z|²-1) through those 16 moments forces the coefficients of |z|², z,zbar,constant to zero, leaving a nonzero harmonic quadratic whose zero set is two perpendicular lines. On each line, three odd moments and <=3 occupied sites force a single equal-weight antipodal pair; from second and fourth moments each line has radius²=2 and contributes sixth moment 2, summing 4 instead of required 6. Thus no-five-node impossibility is analytic, not numerical. At six sites ±sqrt((5±sqrt17)/2), ±i sqrt2 with claimed weights, independently checked all sixteen symbolic moments exactly using SymPy. In the centrally symmetric case, three distinct squared radii and the two even off-diagonal moments force opposite axes and the middle radius²=2; the remaining two-atom real radial moments force roots of s²-5s+2 and unique positive masses, while Vandermonde odd moments force equal within antipodal pairs. Unrestricted six-node uniqueness not claimed.
